texts.preamble: M C Bhatt Food Inspector vs Rajendra Mansukhlal Shah Prop.Ronak ... on 10 April, 2015 Author: Z.K.Saiyed Bench: Z.K.Saiyed R/Cr.A/624/2006 Judgment In The High Court Of Gujarat At Ahmedabad Criminal Appeal No. 624 of 2006 For Approval And Signature: Honourable Mr.Justice Z.K.Saiyed ================================================================ 1 Whether Reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment ? 2 To be referred to the Reporter or not ? 3 Whether their Lordships wish to see the fair copy of the judgment ? 4 Whether this case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution of India or any order made thereunder ? ================================================================ M C Bhatt Food INSPECTOR....Appellant(s) Versus Rajendra Mansukhlal Shah Prop.Ronak Oil Mill Compay & 3....Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) ================================================================ Appearance: Mr Ki Shah, Advocate for the Appellant(s) No. 1 Mr Dk Modi, Advocate for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1 - 3 Mr Md Modi, Advocate for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1 - 3 Mrs Hansa Punani App for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 4 ================================================================ Coram: Honourable Mr.Justice Z.K.Saiyed M C Bhatt Food Inspector vs Rajendra Mansukhlal Shah Prop.Ronak ... on 10 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32370524/ 1 Date : 10/04/2015 Oral Judgment
texts.facts: The said case was registered against the present respondents - original accused for the offence under sections 7(i) and 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "PFA Act"). The said Judgment of the trial Court has been challenged by the appellant on the ground that the Judgment and order passed by learned trial Court is against the law and evidence on record. 2. According to the prosecution case, on 26.2.1999, at about 12:00 p.m. at noon, the appellant - Food Inspector visited the respondent No.2 and at that time, accused No.2 was present and from him, the appellant purchased Micro Refine Kapasia oil in three plastic bottles by paying price of the same. After following due procedure of sealing, packing etc. one sample was sent for analysis purpose. Analyst report revealed the said sample of edible oil was adulterated and therefore, after obtaining sanction under Section 20 of the Act, the complaint was lodged against the accused persons. Therefore, aforesaid Criminal Case was registered.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned advocate Mr. Shah, appearing on behalf of the R/CR.A/624/2006 JUDGMENT appellant has contended that the Judgment and order of acquittal is contrary to law and evidence on record and is not proper. He has contended that learned trial Judge has committed error in acquitting the accused on the ground that the public analyst himself had not tested the sample and he made only signature. He also submitted that the accused were joined without any documents showing their involvement in the business. He has contended that the trial Court has failed to appreciate the report of the Analyst. He has also contended that the offences punishable under the Act are directly connected with the health of public at large. 5. Learned advocate Mr. Modi for the respondents - accused supported the impugned judgment and order of acquittal and he submitted that learned trial Judge has rightly appreciated the evidence produced on record and therefore, no interference is required to be called for. Learned counsel for the appellant is unable to convince this court as to whether the prosecution has followed the mandatory provision of Rules.
